# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-2 (Extended v20)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod attendance); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); **1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—around sunset; Valjean's theft and flight same evening/night)**; present day (spring transitioning to late August/early September, England); future wedding (following spring); **1795 (Jean Valjean's theft at Faverolles and trial at age approximately 25-26)**
- Primary locations: England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford harbor towns, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere); Secondary locations: San Francisco, New York, Eastern Prussia, Germany, Hamburgh; French locations (D——, Manosque, Sisteron, Hautes-Alpes, Paris, Italy, Durance, Château-Arnoux, Senez, Briançon, Aix, Draguignan, Embrun, Chastelar, Arche, Barcelonette, Jauziers, Tuiles, Joug-de-l'Aigle, Ubaye, Ubayette, Ollioules, Nice, Piédmont, Couloubrieux, Cannes, Rue Cassette, Elmhaven, Staveford, Grenoble, Bras d'Asse, Escoublon, Grasse, Franche-Comté, Pontarlier, Lods, Châtillon, Audincourt, Beure, Faverolles, Brie, Tottlingen, Toulon, Quenford, Ravenmere, Basses-Alpes)
- **October 1815 evening/night sequence in D——: Sunset approaching; frost silvered hedges; rain threatening but holding off; salt and tar smell on wind from water; bell for vespers rings; smoke lies flat; baker's boy late, line at oven long; children chase hoop shrieking; cart with turnips creaks past well; gulls quarrel over fish heads; someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall. At supper (eight o'clock): Bishop at table with Valjean, Baptistine, Madame Magloire. After supper: Valjean in alcove bed, struggling with temptation to steal. Post-midnight: Valjean executes theft and flees. Following morning: Bishop at breakfast, remarks contentedly to Baptistine and Madame Magloire about simplicity of bread and milk. As sun declines, three leagues from D——: Valjean sits behind bush on ruddy deserted plain; Alps visible on horizon; bird cries heard; evening chill descends.**

## Main Characters and Relationships

**M. Charles Myriel / Monseigneur Bienvenu / Monseigneur Welcome (Bishop)**
- French aristocrat; family ruined by Revolution; emigrated to Italy; wife died in Italy
- Became priest, then Bishop of D——; encountered Napoleon circa coronation epoch
- Redistributes entire 15,000 franc yearly State salary across 23 charitable categories; retains 1,500 francs yearly for personal sustenance
- Philosophy: society culpable for poverty and ignorance; universe appears as immense malady; strives to dress wounds and relieve suffering
- Attended condemned murderer's execution; experienced deep moral crisis upon return regarding scaffold as monstrous instrument
- Daily life: Sleeps little; morning meditation one hour; says mass; breaks fast on rye bread dipped in milk; at eight o'clock evening, writes; at half-past eight sups extraordinarily frugal repast; after supper converses half hour then retires
- Furniture sparse and austere: six silver knives, forks, and soup-ladle; two large candlesticks of massive silver; iron hospital bed with green serge canopy; bookcase cupboard with glass doors
- Garden: four alleys in cross-form radiating from tank; three plots for vegetables; fourth planted with flowers and fruit-trees
- House has no locked doors day or night; philosophy: "This is the shade of difference: the door of the physician should never be shut, the door of the priest should always be open"
- **Bandit incident: After destruction of Gaspard Bès's band in Ollioules gorges, lieutenant Cravatte took refuge in mountains. Bishop arrived at Chastelar and traveled fortnight preaching. Upon return, large chest deposited by two unknown horsemen containing pontifical vestments stolen from Notre Dame d'Embrun, with paper reading: "From Cravatte to Monseigneur Bienvenu."**
- **1809: Summoned by Napoleon to synod of bishops at Paris**
- **1811 (June 15): Attended synod at Notre-Dame; remarked on luxuries**
- **Political views: Beginning 1813, gave adherence to all hostile manifestations against Napoleon. Refused to see him as he passed through on return from Elba. Acknowledged character flaw: Had his hour of party spirit, bitterness, cloud. Was Royalist.**
- **1815: Reached seventy-fifth birthday; did not appear more than sixty. Rather plump; took long strolls on foot; step firm; form slightly bent.**
- Character: Humble soul loved by all. Inclined towards all that groans and all that expiates. Gazed upon God without seeking to comprehend. Divided leisure between gardening daytime and contemplation night.
- Besides sister Baptistine, had two brothers: one a general, other a prefect. More affectionate correspondence with ex-prefect brother living in retirement at Paris on Rue Cassette.
- **Evening of October 1815: When Valjean confesses his status at supper, Bishop responds with warmth and dignity. Explains fruitières of Pontarlier. After supper, Mother Gerbaud visits with child; Bishop kisses child and borrows fifteen sous to give to Gerbaud. Tells Valjean: "You must be in great need of your bed." Says grace and instructs Madame Magloire to clear table promptly. Later sends goat skin from Black Forest (from Baptistine's room) to Valjean's bed for warmth. Knelt before curtain of alcove concealing altar and said brief prayer. Made strange abrupt movement—folded arms, bent savage gaze upon guest, exclaimed in hoarse voice (words unspecified)—moment of intensity unclear in intent.**
- **Following morning: Bent down examining plant of cochlearia des Guillons broken by fallen basket of silver. Rose up at Madame Magloire's cry. At breakfast, remarked gayly to Baptistine (who said nothing) and Madame Magloire (grumbling under breath) that one does not need fork or spoon, even of wood, to dip bread in milk.**

**Mademoiselle Baptistine** (Bishop's sister)
- Long, pale, thin, gentle creature; embodiment of respectability; acquired beauty of goodness
- Yearly income 500 francs for personal wants
- Witnessed Bishop's deep moral crisis; shares confidence in his openness
- **October 1815 evening: Peaceable and natural; at supper with Valjean. Lends fifteen sous for Mother Gerbaud. Possesses goat skin from Black Forest and little ivory-handled knife.**
- **Following morning: Said nothing at breakfast while Bishop remarked contentedly.**

**Madame Magloire** (Bishop's servant)
- Only servant in household
- Eventually accustomed herself to Bishop's openness
- **October 1815 evening: Heard warnings about prowler of evil appearance—dangerous mendicant in town. Revealed Labarre had not been willing to receive him. Vagabond had been seen arriving via boulevard Gassendi, roaming streets in gloaming. Proposed Bishop permit locksmith Paulin Musebois to replace ancient locks. At supper, placed three sets of forks and spoons; when Bishop has guest, laid out all six silver sets on tablecloth—innocent ostentation. After supper, cleared table very promptly. Later carried goat skin to Valjean's bed. Placed six silver sets in little cupboard near head of bed on right side as you enter from dining-room.**
- **Night of theft: With all vivacity of alert old woman, rushed to oratory, entered alcove, and returned to Bishop to report discovery.**
- **Following morning: Grumbled under breath at breakfast while Bishop remarked contentedly.**

**Jean Valjean**
- **Born in poor peasant family of Brie; did not learn to read in childhood. Became tree-pruner at Faverolles. Mother named Jeanne Mathieu; father called Jean Valjean, probably sobriquet. Lost both parents at very early age. Sister older than himself—widow with seven children—brought him up.**
- **At approximately 25-26 years, took father's place and supported sister. This done simply as duty and churlishly on his part. Youth spent in rude and ill-paid toil.**
- **1795: Theft and trial—One Sunday evening, Maubert Isabeau, baker on Church Square at Faverolles, was preparing for bed when heard violent blow on grated shop front. Arm passed through hole, seized loaf of bread, carried it off. Thief flung away loaf but arm still bleeding. It was Jean Valjean. Taken before tribunals for theft and breaking and entering inhabited house at night. Had gun which he used better than any one else; bit of poacher, which injured his case. Condemned to five years in galleys. Set out for Toulon on cart after 27-day journey.**
- **Imprisonment at Toulon: Clothed in red cassock; all that had constituted his life, even to his name, was effaced; he was number 24,601. Initially believed he was not innocent man unjustly punished, admitted theft was extreme and blameworthy. Over nineteen years, questioned whether he alone was at fault. Reflected society must care for laborers without work. Recognized chastisement ferocious and disproportioned; penalty exceeded culprit's fault. Over-weight of penalty equivalent to annihilation of crime, reversing situation, replacing fault of delinquent with fault of repression, converting guilty man into victim. Penalty, complicated by successive aggravations for four escape attempts, became outrage perpetrated by stronger upon feebler.**
- **Character transformation during imprisonment: Law's effect upon human soul terrible. Pains of brutalizing nature transform man into wild beast. Human society had done him nothing but harm; never seen except angry face called Justice. Men only touched him to bruise him. Every contact had been blow. From suffering to suffering, gradually arrived at conviction that life is war; he was conquered. Had no other weapon than hate. Resolved to whet it in galleys and bear it away when departed.**
- **Escape attempts: Successive obstinate escape attempts prove strange working of law upon human soul. Escaped impetuously like wolf finding cage open. Instinct said "Flee!" In presence of so violent temptation, reason vanished; nothing remained but instinct. Beast alone acted. When recaptured, fresh severities only rendered him more wild.**
- **Physical strength and skill: Possessed physical strength not approached by single galley denizen. Worth four men at work. Sometimes lifted and sustained enormous weights on back. Comrades nicknamed him "Jean the Jack-screw." Once, repairing town-hall balcony at Toulon, supported Puget caryatid with shoulder, giving workmen time to arrive. Suppleness exceeded strength. To climb vertical surface and find support points where barely projection visible was play to Valjean. Could raise himself magically to third story; sometimes mounted even to galley-prison roof.**
- **Emotional state during imprisonment: Spoke little, laughed not at all. Seemed occupied in constant contemplation of something terrible. At times paused and fell to thinking. Reason rose in revolt against perceived absurdity. Said to himself "It is a dream." Gazed at galley-sergeant phantom-like; phantom dealt him blow. Consciousness periodically disappeared and reappeared, fluctuating between awareness and dissociation.**
- **Education: At Toulon, school for convicts kept by Ignorantin friars. Valjean went to school at age 40, learned to read, write, cipher. Felt intelligence fortified his hate. Sentence extended: five years initial plus fourteen years for four escape attempts equals nineteen years total.**
- **Liberation and post-galley experience: Upon liberation heard words, "Thou art free!" Moment seemed improbable and unprecedented. But ray paled. Valjean had been dazzled by idea of liberty; believed in new life. Very speedily perceived what sort of liberty it is to which a yellow passport is provided. This encompassed with much bitterness. Calculated his earnings ought to amount to 171 francs, reduced by various levies to 109 francs fifteen sous. Had understood nothing of this, and thought himself wronged—robbed.**
- **Post-liberation labor: Day following liberation, at Grasse, in front of orange-flower distillery, saw men engaged in unloading bales. Offered services. Business pressing; accepted. He worked intelligently, robustly, adroitly; master seemed pleased. Gendarme passed, observed him, demanded papers. Valjean showed yellow passport. When evening arrived, presented himself to owner for payment. Owner handed him fifteen sous. Valjean objected. Told "That is enough for thee." Persisted. Master looked him straight between eyes and said "Beware of the prison."**
- **Appearance upon arrival at D——, October 1815: Medium stature, thickset and robust, approximately 46 years old. Cap with drooping leather visor; face burned and tanned by sun and wind, dripping with perspiration; coarse yellow linen shirt fastened at neck by small silver anchor; hairy breast; cravat twisted into string; blue drilling trousers worn and threadbare, white on one knee, torn on other; old gray tattered blouse, patched on elbow with bit of green cloth sewn on with twine; soldier knapsack tightly packed on back; enormous knotty stick in hand; iron-shod shoes on stockingless feet; shaved head and long beard.**
- **Disposition: Thoughtful but not gloomy; constituted peculiarity of affectionate natures. Something decidedly sluggish and insignificant about appearance.**
- **October 1815 evening supper: Advanced three paces and approached lamp on table. Stated: "I am a galley-slave; a convict. I come from the galleys." Drew from pocket large sheet of yellow paper, unfolded it—yellow passport to expel him from every place. "I am dangerous man." Overwhelmed when Bishop accepts him; exclaims: "Really? What! You will keep me? You do not drive me forth? A convict! You call me sir! You do not address me as thou? 'Get out of here, you dog!' is what people always say to me. Oh, what a good woman that was who directed me hither! I am going to sup! A bed with a mattress and sheets, like the rest of the world! It is nineteen years since I have slept in a bed!" Recounts he has spent only twenty-five sous in four days, earned by helping unload wagons at Grasse.**
- **Temptation in alcove: Madame Magloire's placing of six silver sets on table haunts him. Observes cupboard location carefully: on right, as you enter from dining-room. Sets are solid old silver. From ladle alone he could get at least two hundred francs—double what he earned in nineteen years. Rationalizes by thinking: "if the _administration_ had not _robbed him_." Mind wavers for a whole hour in fluctuations with which there is mingled some struggle. At three o'clock, opens his eyes again, draws himself up, stretches out arm, feels of knapsack. Removes shoes softly and places them on mat beside bed. Resumes thoughtful attitude. Intrusive thought: Convict named Brevet from galleys, whose trousers upheld by single suspender of knitted cotton; checkered pattern recurs incessantly.**
- **Preparation for theft: Having taken survey, executes movement like man who has made up his mind. Strides to alcove, grasps knapsack, opens it, pulls out object which he places on bed—short bar of iron, pointed like pike at one end: miners' candlestick from Toulon. Puts shoes into pocket, throws knapsack on shoulders, puts on cap, draws visor down, feels for cudgel, places it in angle of window. Resolutely seizes miners' candlestick.**
- **Moment of terror: Fantastical exaggerations of first moment; imagines hinge has assumed terrible life and is barking like dog to arouse every one. Halts shuddering, bewildered; falls back from tips of toes upon heels. Hears arteries in temples beating like two forge hammers. Breath issues from breast with roar of wind issuing from cavern. Impossible to him that horrible clamor of irritated hinge should not have disturbed entire household like shock of earthquake. For a moment thinks himself lost.**
- **Confrontation with Bishop's radiance: Enters Bishop's room; discovers Bishop sleeping peacefully in garment of brown wool, head thrown back on pillow in careless attitude of repose, hand adorned with pastoral ring hanging over edge of bed. At moment when ray of moonlight superposed itself upon inward radiance, sleeping Bishop seemed as in a glory—gentle and veiled in ineffable half-light. Moon, slumbering nature, garden without quiver, calm house, hour, moment, silence added solemn and unspeakable quality to venerable repose; enveloped in serene and majestic aureole that white hair, those closed eyes, that face in which all was hope and all was confidence. Valjean in shadow, motionless, with iron candlestick in hand, frightened by this luminous old man. Never had he beheld anything like this. This confidence terrified him. Moral world has no grander spectacle: troubled and uneasy conscience arriving on brink of evil action, contemplating slumber of the just.**
- **Psychological crisis: No one could have told what was passing within him, not even himself. Haggard astonishment on visage. Gazed at Bishop, and that was all. Strange indecision evident. One would have said that he was hesitating between two abysses—one in which one loses oneself and that in which one saves oneself. Seemed prepared to crush that skull or to kiss that hand.**
- **Execution of theft: Suddenly replaced cap on brow; stepped rapidly past bed without glancing at Bishop, straight to cupboard near head; raised iron candlestick as though to force lock; key was there; opened it; first thing which presented itself was basket of silverware; seized it; traversed chamber with long strides, without taking precautions about noise; gained door; re-entered oratory; opened window; seized cudgel; bestrode window-sill of ground floor; put silver into knapsack; threw away basket; crossed garden; leaped over wall like tiger; fled.**
- **Flight and aftermath: As sun declined, three leagues distant from D——, sat down behind bush on large ruddy plain, absolutely deserted. Alps visible on horizon; not even spire of distant village. Path intersected plain, passed few paces from bush. Only sound: tiny feeble cries of flock of birds of passage traversing heavens at immense height. Child had been standing with back to sun, which cast threads of gold in his hair and empurpled with blood-red gleam the savage face of Jean Valjean. [Claim: child observed and fled from Valjean] Remained standing, not changed attitude after child's flight. Breath heaved his chest at long and irregular intervals. Gaze fixed ten or twelve paces in front, scrutinizing with profound attention shape of ancient fragment of blue earthenware fallen in grass. Suddenly shivered; had just begun to feel chill of evening. At that moment caught sight of forty-sou piece, foot had half ground into earth, shining among pebbles. As though he had received galvanic shock. Recoiled three paces, halted, unable to detach gaze from spot. Darted convulsively towards silver coin, seized it, straightened himself up again, began to gaze afar off over plain, casting eyes towards all points of horizon, erect and shivering, like terrified wild animal seeking refuge.**

## Secondary Characters
- **Labarre**: Landlord of Cross of Colbas inn; man of consideration in town; identified Valjean, drove him away
- **Fishmonger of Rue de Chaffaut**: Encountered Valjean; reported him to Labarre
- **Mother Gerbaud**: Visited Bishop at supper with little child; received fifteen sous from Baptistine via Bishop's instruction
- Paulin Musebois: Locksmith
- Marie-Claude: Farmer's wife at Faverolles; lent milk to Valjean's siblings
- Jeanne Mathieu (Valjean's mother); Jean Valjean (Valjean's father); Valjean's sister; Maubert Isabeau: Baker; Gaspard Bès: Bandit; Lieutenant Cravatte: Bandit; Ignorantin friars; Brevet: Convict at Toulon; Puget: Sculptor of caryatids
- **Volia Brackick**: By trade weaver; born at Dunstead [no relation to other Brackick mentioned in earlier summary established]

## Themes
- Redemptive mercy and Christian charity; transformative power of acceptance and dignity restoration
- Possibility of redemption and restoration of divine spark despite prolonged dehumanization
- Temptation and moral struggle following acceptance and kindness
- Radiance of virtue confronting darkness of desperation
- Hesitation between self-destruction and self-salvation
- Theft following Christian mercy; silver represents restitution for "stolen" wages from galleys
- Flight and psychological fragmentation post-crime
- Intrusive convict memories and trauma imprints
- Divine presence and its terrifying effect on corrupted soul
